meta.scope: Bounded scoping review (not systematic). No reproducible protocol. Not a systematic review.

evidence.title: Self-Damaging Contrastive Learning (SDCLR)
evidence.design: Dynamic self-competitor: a pruned copy of the target model is contrasted with it; samples the pruned model forgets (tail-like) are implicitly up-weighted in the contrastive loss. Framework: SimCLR (not MoCo). Extra cost: one additional forward pass of the pruned model.
evidence.dataset: CIFAR10-LT, CIFAR100-LT, ImageNet-100-LT; balanced CIFAR10/100 as control.
evidence.baseline: SimCLR, same backbone and linear-probe protocol.
evidence.result: Linear probe (Table 4, full-line extraction): CIFAR10-LT SimCLR 75.55 +/- 0.66 -> SDCLR 82.00 +/- 0.68 (+6.45 pp). Few-shot-class group 71.37 -> 76.23. CIFAR100-LT +8.37 pp (text). ImageNet-100-LT +1.02 pp (text). Balanced CIFAR10 accuracy 91.16 -> 91.55 (Table 6). Few-shot linear (Table 5, CIFAR10) All 67.08 -> 70.47.
evidence.which_class: Groups many/medium/few reported; no per-class dermatology result.
evidence.fulltext_or_abstract: Full text, PARTIAL extraction (tables 4-6 and section 4.4-4.6 passages). Not a complete sequential read.
evidence.limitation: SimCLR on CIFAR/ImageNet subsets, not MoCo; not dermatology; number of seeds shown as +/- std from repeated runs (seed count not verified in extraction); the 'few' gain is a group mean, not a per-class recall; the pruned-model mechanism adds a hyperparameter (dropout/pruning ratio 0.9 mentioned in text).
evidence.relevance_to_us: Strongest label-free rare-class SSL evidence found with numbers. Transferable idea: a second, pruned/momentum-lagged key encoder as a hardness signal inside MoCo. Cost roughly +1 forward per step on GPU0. Ranked R3 for SSL, not first, because it changes the loss and not only the sampler.

evidence.title: Self-supervised Learning is More Robust to Dataset Imbalance (Liu, HaoChen, Gaidon, Ma)
evidence.design: Analysis that off-the-shelf SSL is already more robust to imbalance than supervised learning; proposes re-weighted regularization (rwSAM) where per-sample weight = inverse kernel density of the representation (no labels), applied through a reweighted sharpness-aware step.
evidence.dataset: CIFAR-10-LT (step and exponential imbalance); ImageNet-LT pre-training with fine-tuning on downstream sets.
evidence.baseline: SimSiam and MoCo v2; SSL balanced with same number of examples.
evidence.result: Text: rwSAM improves SimSiam by over 1% linear-probe on CIFAR-10-LT and surpasses SimSiam on balanced CIFAR-10 with the same number of examples; rare-example generalization gap 0.081 -> 0.066. Table 1b: improves MoCo v2 and SimSiam fine-tuning on ImageNet-LT downstream (table numbers not extracted).
evidence.which_class: Rare-example gap reported; no per-class dermatology result.
evidence.fulltext_or_abstract: Full text, PARTIAL extraction (Section 4 results, Table 1 caption and text). Table 1 numeric cells not extracted.
evidence.limitation: Gains reported as ~1 pp on CIFAR-10-LT; rwSAM doubles the gradient cost (two passes); KDE bandwidth h and alpha chosen by cross-validation on the same benchmarks; the MoCo result is fine-tuning, not linear readout.
evidence.relevance_to_us: Best-documented label-free way to get a density-based reweighting of the SSL pool, including MoCo v2 results. Compute ~2x per step. Used as PhB.

evidence.title: Divide and Contrast: Self-supervised Learning from Uncurated Data (DnC)
evidence.design: Alternates contrastive learning with clustering-based hard-negative mining; hypothesis that heavy-tailed uncurated data yields less relevant negatives.
evidence.dataset: YFCC and other uncurated sets vs ImageNet.
evidence.baseline: Contrastive learning on uncurated data without DnC.
evidence.result: Abstract only: DnC greatly improves SSL on less-curated data, competitive on curated data.
evidence.limitation: Numbers not verified; clustering is a periodic offline step.
evidence.relevance_to_us: Supports cluster structure as a label-free signal for pool curation. Cited as context for PhA (clusters from the SSL pool).

evidence.title: Temperature Schedules for Self-Supervised Contrastive Methods on Long-Tail Data
evidence.design: Cosine schedule for the contrastive temperature tau (large tau = group-wise discrimination, small tau = instance discrimination).
evidence.result: Abstract only: consistent gains in class separation at no cost.
evidence.limitation: Temperature arms are ALREADY in the brief's negative list (SSL hyperparameter arms: temperature). Low priority unless the earlier temperature arm used a schedule.
evidence.relevance_to_us: Likely redundant with the already-measured negative temperature arm; check which temperature variant was tested before re-running.

evidence.title: On the Effectiveness of Out-of-Distribution Data in Self-Supervised Long-Tail Learning (COLT)
evidence.design: Online OOD sampling with tailness scores from feature neighborhoods, plus a distribution-level supervised contrastive term to separate ID vs OOD.
evidence.baseline: SSL on long-tail ID data; prior work with external ID data.
evidence.result: Abstract only: large SSL gains on long-tailed sets, outperforms prior work using external ID data.
evidence.limitation: Needs an external OOD pool; the 'distribution-level supervised contrastive loss' name suggests labels or pseudo-labels for ID/OOD split; not confirmed label-free in full.
evidence.relevance_to_us: Not recommended now: requires a second data pool we do not have for dermatology (ISIC/PAD pools are the only ones in scope). Noted as an alternative if an external dermoscopy pool were allowed.

evidence.title: Frequency-Aware Self-Supervised Long-Tailed Learning
evidence.design: Learns frequency-aware prototypes without labels or class frequencies; self-supervised scheme focused on rare-class samples.
evidence.result: Abstract only: qualitative and quantitative improvement claimed.
evidence.limitation: Numbers unknown; venue is a workshop (ICCVW 2023).
evidence.relevance_to_us: Prototype-based label-free alternative to PhA. Lower priority: needs a new loss term and unverified numbers.

evidence.title: Dataset Awareness is not Enough: Sample-level Tail Encouragement in Long-tailed SSL
evidence.design: Uses pseudo-labels to drive per-sample temperature and re-weighting.
evidence.limitation: Pseudo-labels from a classifier: not label-free in the strict Track A sense.

evidence.title: Long-tail learning via logit adjustment (Menon et al.)
evidence.label_free: reader-side (uses labels for the training prior; readout labels are required by necessity)
evidence.design: Post-hoc logit adjustment: at test time subtract tau * log(pi_y) from logits (pi_y = class prior); or the same adjustment enforced in the training loss. Single scalar tau in the post-hoc form.
evidence.result: Abstract only: two simple modifications that unify and improve prior methods; cited 677 times in OpenAlex.
evidence.which_class: Relative margin between rare and dominant labels (abstract).
evidence.limitation: Our readout is balanced LR (already a prior correction, roughly tau=1 in the logit form); the post-hoc gain is therefore a recall-precision trade along tau, not new information. The brief reports per-class inner-tuned offsets as negative; a single tau has far fewer degrees of freedom.
evidence.relevance_to_us: Basis of reader recipe R4 (single-tau adjustment on the readout, tuned in inner grouped CV).

evidence.title: Balanced Meta-Softmax for Long-Tailed Visual Recognition
evidence.design: Balanced Softmax: training-time softmax with the class prior in the denominator (unbiased under label-distribution shift).
evidence.limitation: Requires retraining a head with the prior in the loss; on a frozen-feature LR readout it reduces to a logit offset equivalent to R4 with tau fixed to 1.
evidence.relevance_to_us: Equivalent to R4 with tau=1 on frozen features; no separate recipe needed.

evidence.title: BCL, TSC, NCL, ProCo, Reb-SupCon (long-tailed contrastive)
evidence.design: Supervised contrastive losses using class labels.
evidence.limitation: Supervised; outside Track A. Listed to make the exclusion explicit.
evidence.relevance_to_us: Track B at most. Not used as evidence for SSL recommendations.

evidence.title: Curricular SSL for skin lesions; self-supervised multi-modality multi-label skin lesion classification with cluster pseudo-labels
evidence.design: Dermatology SSL pretraining; the 2025 paper uses k-means-style clustering to make surrogate pseudo-multi-labels.
evidence.result: Abstract only: curriculum of pretext tasks beats ImageNet pretraining on ISIC-2019.
evidence.limitation: No minority-class recall under imbalance is reported; not a balancing method.
evidence.relevance_to_us: Context only: dermatology SSL exists, none measures melanoma-vs-nevus recall under imbalance.

evidence.title: Dynamically Weighted Balanced Loss (DWB) for imbalanced learning, incl. ISIC2019
evidence.result: Abstract only: superior empirical performance on ISIC2019.
evidence.limitation: Supervised training loss; not applicable to a frozen readout without retraining.
evidence.relevance_to_us: Derm context only for a loss-side alternative (not recommended now).

evidence.title: Systematic Failure of Vision Transformers in Imbalanced Skin Lesion Classification
evidence.design: ViT-Base trained from scratch on ISIC 2019 with class-balanced CE.
evidence.result: Abstract only: test accuracy 8.0-37.8%, minority F1 < 0.05 despite class-balanced loss.
evidence.limitation: From-scratch training with no SSL; not comparable to our frozen DINOv2-based MoCo.
evidence.relevance_to_us: Caution: class-balanced loss alone is not sufficient without representation-level balance when data are scarce.

evidence.title: Improving Representation Learning for Long-Tailed Visual Recognition (IRLS)
evidence.design: Contrastive long-tail loss with class-wise mean-vector-norm guidance and an outlier-aware module; uses class labels.
evidence.limitation: Supervised; no dermatology evidence; 0 citations at retrieval.
evidence.relevance_to_us: Track B at most; not used.

recipes_ranked.name: Cluster-balanced sampler on the SSL pool (inverse cluster-size sampling, sqrt-balanced)
algorithm: Every R epochs (R=5 default) and at epoch 0: encode the SSL pool with the current MoCo query encoder (no augmentation; CLS4 pre-projection, L2-normalised), giving F in R^{N x d}.
Reduce X = PCA(F, 128), then L2-normalise rows (spherical geometry).
c = KMeans(K, n_init=3, random_state=seed) on X; K=64 default. If any cluster size < 10, reduce K by merging the smallest into their nearest centroid (or use K=32).
n_k = |{i: c_i = k}|; per-sample weight w_i = n_{c_i}^(-alpha); alpha=0.5 default (arms: alpha in {0, 0.5, 1.0}); p_i = w_i / sum_j w_j.
Sampler: WeightedRandomSampler(weights=p, num_samples=N, replacement=True, generator=seeded). Replaces the uniform shuffle only; MoCo queue, key encoder and loss are UNCHANGED.
Log per refresh: K, min/max cluster size, normalised entropy of cluster-sampling distribution, fraction of pool in the largest cluster (warn if > 0.5).
recipes_ranked.clustering_stability_gate: Run KMeans with 2 seeds; ARI between the two partitions must be >= 0.5 at the refresh epoch, else keep the previous partition and log it.
recipes_ranked.confound_diagnostic: OFFLINE ONLY (never used in training): NMI between clusters and acquisition metadata (device/phase/site) on ham_dev and pad_adapt. If clusters mostly encode acquisition (high NMI, to be set by the SSL engineer), PhA can only re-balance acquisition, not disease classes. Discard the arm in that case.
recipes_ranked.expected_effect: Modest. Mechanism: rare visual modes get more gradient steps. Probability (subjective, ~30%) of a seed-consistent gain on melanoma recall (HAM mel recall, PAD MEL recall) with macro-F1 non-decreasing; ~60% chance the effect is within the seed noise of the brief's readout (no change). Low chance of large gains (>3 pp) on SCC.
recipes_ranked.compute: Feature pass over the pool every 5 epochs (forward only) + KMeans on N x 128 (CPU seconds for N in the low thousands; check the pool size before estimating GPU time). No extra training FLOPs. Use GPU0 for the pass; CPU readouts <=3 BLAS threads.
recipes_ranked.arms: A: uniform (baseline, already measured) | B: alpha=0.5 | C: alpha=1.0. Seeds 42/43/44 at 224 px, 1 view; compare with baseline refit in the same environment. Endpoints as in the internal research brief.
self_checks: Sampler weights sum to 1; sampled cluster histogram matches predicted p within 3% over 10k draws.
Same seed reproduces identical sampled indices.
Collision audit (brief: same-component collisions 0.49%) re-run for cluster-balanced batches; report if it rises above 2%.
recipes_ranked.risks: Clusters may encode imaging artefacts (rulers, vignetting, background), which the CAMEO abstract flags as a candidate HAM mel error source. Oversampling small clusters amplifies noise in those clusters.
evidence: E3 (abstract: cluster-based curation helps SSL on uncurated data)
E2 (full text partial: density-based weights without labels help SSL on imbalance)
recipes_ranked.evidence_strength: Moderate-low. The sampler itself has no direct primary evidence in a MoCo setup; it is a combination of E2/E3 mechanisms.

recipes_ranked.name: Density-reweighted SSL objective (rwSAM-style) on the MoCo pool
recipes_ranked.target: cluster-ssl (only if PhA is flat or if a loss-side change is allowed)
algorithm: Per-sample weight w_i = (mean_j K_h(f_i - f_j))^(-alpha) with Gaussian kernel K_h on L2-normalised features, computed from the current batch or a memory bank (E2).
Reweighted sharpness-aware step: eps = rho * grad(sum_i w_i * loss_i) / ||grad||; update with the unweighted loss at theta + eps.
Hyperparameters from E2: rho and alpha selected by CV; use the paper's ranges as a starting point, not as a verified recipe for DINOv2 ViT-B/14.
recipes_ranked.expected_effect: Small. E2 reports about +1 pp linear probe on CIFAR-10-LT with SimSiam, not a dermatology number. Probability of a macro-F1 gain > 0.5 pp in our setting: ~25% (subjective).
recipes_ranked.compute: About 2x forward/backward per step (SAM double pass) plus a kernel density over the batch. Roughly doubles SSL wall time. Only worth it if PhA gives a signal.
recipes_ranked.evidence_strength: Moderate for the mechanism in SimSiam/MoCo v2 (E2, full text partial); low for our task.

recipes_ranked.name: SDCLR-style pruned self-competitor as a hardness signal (MoCo key-encoder variant)
algorithm: Keep a pruned copy of the key encoder (magnitude pruning at a fixed ratio, e.g. 0.9 as in E1 text, or dropout-as-pruning).
Contrast the target with the pruned self-competitor; samples whose loss changes most after pruning receive more weight in the contrastive loss (E1).
recipes_ranked.expected_effect: Largest reported gain in the set (+6.45 pp linear CIFAR10-LT, SimCLR, E1), but in SimCLR on CIFAR and with no dermatology evidence. Expected effect for DINOv2 MoCo: uncertain; ~20% chance of a clear macro-F1 gain at a cost of one extra forward pass.
recipes_ranked.compute: About +1 forward per step; plus an extra hyperparameter sweep (pruning ratio).
recipes_ranked.evidence_strength: Moderate for the mechanism (E1 full text, partial extraction); low for transfer.

recipes_ranked.name: Reader-side single-tau logit adjustment on the balanced LR readout, decision by inner-CV macro-F1
algorithm: Fit the existing balanced LR (row-L2, grouped folds unchanged) on frozen features.

For each candidate tau in a fixed grid (e.g. -0.5, -0.25, 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0), compute adjusted logits z_c' = z_c + tau * log(pi_c) (Menon post-hoc form; pi_c = training-fold class prior). tau=0 is the current readout.

Choose tau and C jointly by inner grouped CV macro-F1 (never on the outer fold or on HAM holdout / PAD target_test), then report the full curve of mel recall vs nv precision and SCC recall vs BCC/ACK, not only the chosen point.
Report seed-wise deltas; decision rule must be stated before running.
recipes_ranked.expected_effect: Recall-precision trade along tau: melanoma/SCC recall up, nevus/BCC precision down. Macro-F1 gain is bounded because balanced LR already corrects the prior. Probability of a macro-F1 gain > 0.5 pp: ~25%; probability of minority recall gain without macro-F1 loss > 1 pp: ~35% (subjective).
recipes_ranked.compute: CPU only, seconds per fold; within the <=3 BLAS-thread limit.
recipes_ranked.evidence_strength: Low for dermatology (no derm logit-adjustment result found, S10/S11). Moderate for the general mechanism (E8, abstract only; full text not read).
recipes_ranked.executed_result: NEGATIVE ( reader-imbalance, docs/reader-gap-r4.json, pre-registered rule). Verified in that JSON: joint (tau,C) macro-F1 deltas per encoder seed within about -0.006 to +0.007; no block meets the rule. HAM 224 seed-mean delta -0.0157. Monotone trade-off confirmed: HAM 448 mel->NV ~0.19 at tau 0 falls to ~0.07 at tau 1, mel recall +0.02, macro-F1 ~0.61 -> ~0.50 (mean of 3 seeds). PAD 224 deltas reach +0.005 to +0.007, but minority recall falls. Do not repeat this arm.

recipes_ranked.name: Balanced Softmax / class-balanced loss on the readout
recipes_ranked.algorithm: Equivalent to R4 with tau fixed to 1 on a frozen-feature LR; a separate class-balanced loss would only re-weight the same prior. Not recommended as a separate arm.
recipes_ranked.expected_effect: Overlaps R4; expect no new information.

decision_metric_notes: C selection and tau selection should use inner grouped CV macro-F1 (or macro balanced accuracy) on dev cohorts only. Accuracy is not acceptable: it rewards majority classes.

Report HAM mel recall and mel->nv, PAD MEL recall, SCC recall and SCC->BCC as separate endpoints with per-class precision; the brief's earlier per-class offset result was negative, so a single-tau variant is the only reader arm proposed.
Per-class offsets already tested in this project are not repeated; R4 has one degree of freedom instead of seven.
gaps: No dermatology paper with melanoma-vs-nevus or SCC-vs-BCC recall under label-free SSL reweighting was found.
arXiv search returned zero results for all four queries; the arXiv route was used only for full-text reads of IDs already known from OpenAlex. Coverage of arXiv-only work is therefore unknown.
No paper found that evaluates cluster-balanced sampling specifically in a MoCo pipeline; PhA is a derived recipe, not a replicated method.
Menon 2021 and Liu 2022 numeric tables were not extracted in full; numbers for those items are abstract or partial-text only.
The SDCLR and Liu full texts were read partially by targeted extraction; a complete sequential read is still owed before quoting tables in the thesis.
